title: SAP A2A and MCP interoperability reference architecture
problem: Let Joule agents and third-party agents interoperate with governed access to SAP and non-SAP tools.
depth: Primary SAP documentation; this session used search excerpts, full page body to be read before walkthrough
technologies_stated: SAP Cloud Identity Services App2App tokens with named user context
MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite
facts: SAP uses A2A as the preferred approach for external agent interoperability and MCP for tool access.
The Agent Gateway exposes Joule agents externally via A2A; authentication uses IAS App2App tokens with named user context.
MCP Gateway in Integration Suite exposes SAP and non-SAP APIs as governed MCP tools.
Inbound A2A interoperability general availability was announced for October 2026; the customer defines which agents a client may invoke.
interpretations: Named-user context in tokens suggests the design intends user-level authorisation across agent hops; confirm in full documentation.
unknown: Full flows and limits (page body not read this session)

decisions.selected: A2A for agent to agent, MCP for tools
decisions.alternatives: Proprietary SAP APIs only; REST per integration
decisions.reasoning: Source states A2A as preferred for external interoperability.

review_exercise: Draw inbound and outbound flows and mark every identity hop.
lessons: Protocol layering: MCP for tools, A2A for agents.
adaptation: Foundation for any BYO-agent SAP engagement.
